lesson_title: The R25 Water Bottle: Value, Utility and Markets
hook_text: Same bottle. R7 outside the stadium. R25 inside. Nothing changed — except you.
clip_script: Same bottle of water: R7 at the supermarket, R25 inside the stadium on a hot match day. The water didn't change. YOU did — thirsty, hot, locked in with no options. Satisfaction lives in the person, not the product; economists call it utility. And it unlocks a riddle that's puzzled people for centuries: water keeps you ALIVE and costs almost nothing. A diamond does nothing vital and costs a fortune. How? Because trading-worth doesn't run on nobility — it runs on SCARCITY. Water is everywhere; another glass, when you have plenty, barely matters. Diamonds are rare; even one more is a big deal. Plenty makes cheap. Scarce makes dear. And the stadium proves it in reverse: lock the gates, and water inside becomes scarce — price tripled. Next time you pay R25 for water, you're not being robbed. You're living inside the oldest riddle in economics — solved.
visual_style: A split scene: supermarket shelf versus stadium stand, the same bottle glowing with different price tags; then a scale weighing a water drop against a diamond, tipping on a SCARCITY weight; gates slamming shut as the price ticks up.
mood: Playful riddle energy with a satisfying click of insight.
pacing: Quick setup, riddle posed, beat of suspense, clean resolution.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and classify every market on your street.
